data.title: Clearing out my parents' house was a legal nightmare. How can I downsize without putting my kids through the same ordeal?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Some countercultural advice this Black Friday: stop buying stuff, plus other rules for downsizing

"Legal fees ended up eating up half the value of my parents' estate." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I have recently read and heard a lot about the recommendation for seniors to take an active role in managing their estates - specifically by downsizing, in addition to having the wills and estate plans you have advised for years. Downsizing means going through all the "stuff" accumulated over the years and weeding out the treasures and clutter we no longer use, need or want.

While many seniors do this when they move into a retirement community, plenty of us stay put in our homes for decades. My parents lived in their home from 1950 to 2020. They believed their children would enjoy going through their belongings and reminiscing after they passed, but the reality was quite different and a massive hassle.

None of us lived nearby, we argued over what to do with 70 years' worth of possessions, and eventually, lawyers and the courts got involved. Legal fees ate up half the value of my parents' estate. Downsizing is difficult because of sentimental attachments, the sheer physical energy it requires and the challenge of knowing what is valuable versus what to let go of.

In my own downsizing efforts, I've avoided the hassle of online listings, garage sales or hiring estate experts, opting instead to give things to neighbors, donate them to Goodwill or toss them. What advice can you share for seniors who have too much stuff, feel overwhelmed by the process and want to spare their families what mine went through?

Aging Downsizer

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: My husband wants to sell our $1.5 million home and downsize. But this is where we raised our kids - and I can't bear to leave.

You will be surprised how quickly you forget about items once they're gone.

Dear Downsizer,

Sticky notes on furniture is no substitute for a proper will.

Your experience clearing out your parents' home is a cautionary tale. Hiring lawyers can cost a fortune and escalate disagreements that could be better resolved with a mediator. When it comes to family, going to court should be the very last resort. Aging parents can start giving away their valuable items to their children in an effort to prevent arguments later on, or put in place a system for choosing them, such as labeling items or drawing straws and allowing each child to choose an item in rotation.

Be aware that giving away expensive antiques, jewelry, or furniture during your lifetime with a combined value exceeding $19,000 per recipient in a single calendar year will require you to file a gift-tax return (IRS Form 709), even though you won't actually owe taxes unless you exceed the multi-million-dollar lifetime exemption. An important sticky note for your estate plans: Naming a third party as executor, and giving them authority in your will to sell any items your children can't agree upon within, say, 30 days, will help keep any family disputes out of court.

Without further ado - and I hope this helps you - here are some tips for clearing your house:

5 rules of downsizing

(1) Be tough. Without throwing out something valuable like an antique, a letter from a loved one or a wedding photo album that can never be replaced, you have to be ruthless when downsizing. And while the struggle is real, you need to avoid engaging in it every time you open a box. Your memories are not packed away in an attic or basement. They are in your mind and they are in your heart.

(2) Think digital. After you have had the hard conversations with your children about what they want or what they don't want, you can take photos of a treasured childhood toy before donating it or throwing it in the garbage. And a Kindle or the Apple Books app takes up less space than thousands of physical books.You can always put your favorite memories on social media or put them in a shared online folder so family members have access to them.

(3) Take it easy. The emotional labor is as challenging as the physical labor. You are, after all, sifting through your memories, which will bring up good and possibly also bad or painful moments. Take your time. You acquired these belongings over a lifetime, so why would you put yourself through the onerous task of dismantling your life in a week or a month? Commit to one big garbage bag per day. If you do two per day, take Sunday off.

(4) Out of sight, out of mind. You will be surprised how quickly you forget about items once they're gone. Anyone who has moved house and lived without their belongings for a period of time will have experienced this. Our stuff becomes part of our identity. Sure, everyone has their own treasures - a piece of artwork that won't take up too much space on a wall - but you may be surprised how quickly you forget about items once they're out of sight.

The emotional labor is often as challenging as the physical labor.

(5) Stop buying. Some countercultural advice this Black Friday - stop buying stuff that replaces the stuff you threw out. Perhaps it's that 2026 holiday sweater that looks so enticing online, even when we have a closet full of old sweaters crying out to be worn. We all love a bargain, and Black Friday and Cyber Monday tempt us to spend, spend, spend (analysts forecast spending nearing $30 billion for both "consumer holidays" this year). Don't replace the stuff you throw out.

Make spring cleaning an annual or semiannual event. As writer Evelyn Richards noted in this personal reflection in Country Living Magazine about downsizing from a three-bedroom house to a one-bedroom apartment: "Decluttering isn't just about tidying up your home; it's also about nurturing your mental well-being. When you clear out the excess and organize your space, you create a serene and stress-free environment."

It feels lighter to walk into a room where everything is in order, she writes. "This kind of order can significantly reduce anxiety and make it easier to relax. When your home is clutter-free, it's like a breath of fresh air, allowing you to focus on what truly matters. Moreover, the process of decluttering itself can be therapeutic. As you sort through items, you make decisions about what to keep and what to let go, which can be incredibly empowering."

I'm resisting buying yet another pair of sneakers this Black Friday because, like you, I have too much stuff. I sometimes wonder how much money I would have saved in my life had I stuck to a black cashmere turtleneck like Apple's late CEO Steve Jobs or a black leather jacket like Nvidia's newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang. You have accumulated a lifetime of memories - and, presumably, a few savvy investments in artwork and furniture - and passing those treasures on to loved ones should be a joy. Still, even the most discerning consumer ends up with clutter.

The ceramic bunny rabbit has got to go.

Related: This is the best Black Friday purchase I ever made

data.title: Southwest Heritage Bank Announces Acquisition Agreement with Peak Credit Union
data.description:
SCOTTSDALE, AZ / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Southwest Heritage Bank, together with the bank's parent company, Bancorp 34, Inc. (OTCID:BCTF), today announced a definitive agreement for Peak Credit Union ("Peak") to acquire Southwest Heritage Bank. Under the agreement, Peak would acquire substantially all of Southwest Heritage Bank's assets and assume substantially all of its liabilities in an all-cash transaction.

The transaction was unanimously approved by the boards of directors of Peak Credit Union, Southwest Heritage Bank, and Bancorp 34, Inc. The acquisition is subject to customary regulatory and stockholder approvals and is expected to be completed in the second half of 2027. Following completion of the transaction, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. will dissolve and the remaining assets will be distributed to the stockholders of Bancorp 34, Inc. Subject to the terms of the agreement, stockholders are expected to receive an estimated $20.67 to $22.18 per share for an aggregate transaction value of $ 159 million to $171 million.

Peak intends to retain members of Southwest Heritage Bank's executive leadership team in senior roles within the combined organization, drawing on their expertise and experience to guide a successful integration and contribute to the credit union's long-term growth and strategic direction. In particular, Southwest Heritage Bank President Paul Tees will be responsible for leading commercial banking across the combined organization, bringing the bank's commercial lending expertise and local-market-led, relationship focused approach to Peak's broader network.

Peak also intends to retain all Southwest Heritage Bank employees immediately upon closing, subject to ordinary business and individual circumstances, to ensure continuity of service and the successful integration of the organizations' systems and processes.

Until the transaction closes, both organizations will continue to operate independently, and there is nothing customers or members need to do.

D.A. Davidson & Co. served as financial advisor and Otteson Shapiro LLP served as legal counsel to Bancorp 34, Inc. and Southwest Heritage Bank. McQueen Financial Advisors served as financial advisor and Luse Gorman, PC served as legal counsel to Peak Credit Union.

Investor Contact: Kevin Vaughn, CFO, 623-334-6064. BCTF@swhb.com

About Bancorp 34, Inc.

Bancorp 34, Inc. is the holding company for Southwest Heritage Bank. The bank's headquarters are located at 8777 East Hartford Drive, Suite 100, Scottsdale, Arizona 85255. In addition, the bank operates seven full-service community bank branches, two in Maricopa County, Arizona, in the cities of Scottsdale and Gilbert; three in Pima County, Arizona, in the cities of Tucson and Green Valley; one branch in Otero County, New Mexico in the city of Alamogordo; and one branch in Dona Ana County New Mexico, in the city of Las Cruces.

About Peak Credit Union

About Peak Credit Union: Peak Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative serving more than 250,000 members through 35 branches across Washington and Oregon and digital banking services. Formed from the combination of TwinStar Credit Union and Northwest Community Credit Union, Peak brings a longstanding commitment to financial education, accessible financial services and community well-being. Through the PeakCU Foundation, Peak supports local initiatives including classroom grants, scholarships and financial education. Federally insured by NCUA. Equal Housing Opportunity. Learn more at peakcu.org.

data.title: Ranchero Gold Announces Change of Auditor, Property Option Amendment, and Grant of Restricted Share Units
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Ranchero Gold Corp. ("Ranchero" or the "Company") (TSX.V:RNCH) announces that Smythe LLP, Chartered Professional Accountants (the "Former Auditor"), has resigned as auditor of the Company effective November 24, 2026, and that the Board of Directors has appointed Truster Zweig Raithatha LLP ("TZR"), as successor auditor effective the same date. TZR will hold office until the close of the Company's next annual meeting of shareholders, at which shareholders will be asked to approve its appointment.

The change was considered by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board. There were no modified opinions in the Former Auditor's reports for the financial years ended December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025, and there have been no "reportable events" as defined in National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations ("NI 51-102"). The Notice of Change of Auditor, together with the response letters of the Former Auditor and TZR, will be filed on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca) in accordance with NI 51-102.

The Company thanks Smythe LLP for its services and looks forward to working with TZR.

Sandspit Option Amendment

Ranchero has also amended its option agreement dated February 28, 2025 with Homegold Resources Ltd. and Johan Thom Shearer for the Sandspit Gold Project on Moresby Island, Haida Gwaii, British Columbia. The final $100,000 option payment, previously due by February 28, 2027, has been restructured as $6,000 due by that date and $100,000 due by February 28, 2028, extending the option period by twelve months. Total cash consideration is now $118,000, of which $12,000 has been paid. The amendment also updates the claim schedule: the property comprises five mineral claims totaling 166 hectares, compared with the 398 hectares previously reported, following a reduction in the area of tenure 1120426. All other terms are unchanged.

Grant of Restricted Share Units

The Company also announces that it has granted 4,150,000 restricted share units ("RSUs") to certain directors and officers of the Company under its Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan. The RSUs vest twelve (12) months from the date of grant and, once vested, will be settled in common shares of the Company, subject to the terms and conditions of the Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan.

Martyn Buttenshaw, a director of the Company and a "qualified person" under National Instrument 43-101, has reviewed and approved the technical information in this news release.

About Ranchero Gold

Ranchero is an exploration and development company currently focused on early-stage gold exploration. Ranchero has the option to earn a 100% interest in the Sandspit gold project, consisting of five mineral claims totalling 166 hectares, situated immediately south of Sandspit, Haida Gwaii, off the coast of British Columbia, Canada. The Company continues to look for additional projects to add to its portfolio.

data.title: Peak Credit Union Announces Agreement to Acquire Southwest Heritage Bank
data.description:
Peak Credit Union Announces Agreement to Acquire Southwest Heritage Bank

Peak Credit Union Announces Agreement to Acquire Southwest Heritage Bank

PR Newswire

EUGENE, Ore. and LACEY, Wash. and SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Nov. 27, 2026

The proposed acquisition would deepen business banking expertise and expand Peak's reach into Arizona and New Mexico

EUGENE, Ore. and LACEY, Wash. and SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Peak Credit Union announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all assets and assume all liabilities of Southwest Heritage Bank, a subsidiary of Bancorp 34, Inc. (OTC: BCTF), in an all-cash transaction.

The proposed acquisition would bring together Peak's broad consumer financial services and member-owned cooperative model with Southwest Heritage's commercial lending expertise, treasury management services, and established business relationships across Arizona and New Mexico. The combination is intended to expand the financial resources available to individuals and business owners while preserving the local expertise and personal relationships valued by Southwest Heritage customers.

"Our focus is on finding meaningful ways to serve more people," said Dr. David L. Tuyo II, president and CEO of Peak Credit Union. "We know many of our members already spend part of the year in Arizona, making it a natural place for us to grow. Southwest Heritage has built trusted relationships with local businesses, backed by people who understand their communities. Bringing that expertise together with Peak's broader capabilities gives us an opportunity to help more people and businesses move toward their financial goals."

Over time, Peak members could benefit from deeper commercial lending and treasury management capabilities, while Southwest Heritage customers could gain access to additional consumer financial services. Specific products, eligibility, and timing will be determined as integration planning progresses.

The employees and relationships of Southwest Heritage Bank are central to the value of the planned transition. Peak intends to retain Southwest Heritage employees at closing, subject to ordinary business and individual circumstances, to support service continuity and integration. Peak also intends to retain members of Southwest Heritage's executive leadership team in senior roles. Final roles and reporting relationships remain subject to approval and integration planning.

There are no immediate changes to branch operations, accounts, or banking services as a result of today's announcement. Until the transaction closes, the two organizations are expected to continue to operate independently, and members and customers do not need to take any action. It is expected that Peak will communicate any future changes directly and in advance.

The boards of directors of Peak Credit Union, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. approved the agreement unanimously. The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory and shareholder approvals and is expected to close in the second half of 2027.

Following closing, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. is expected to dissolve and distribute the remaining assets of Bancorp 34, Inc. to its shareholders in accordance with the transaction terms.

D.A. Davidson & Co. served as financial advisor and Otteson Shapiro LLP served as legal counsel to Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. McQueen Financial Advisors served as financial advisor and Luse Gorman, PC served as legal counsel to Peak Credit Union.

About Peak Credit Union: Peak Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative serving more than 250,000 members through 35 branches across Washington and Oregon and digital banking services. Formed from the combination of TwinStar Credit Union and Northwest Community Credit Union, Peak brings a longstanding commitment to financial education, accessible financial services and community well-being. Through the PeakCU Foundation, Peak supports local initiatives including classroom grants, scholarships and financial education. Federally insured by NCUA. Equal Housing Opportunity. Learn more at peakcu.org.

About Southwest Heritage Bank: Southwest Heritage Bank, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a community-focused bank serving individuals and businesses in Arizona and New Mexico. The bank offers commercial lending, treasury management and personal financial services, with an emphasis on local relationships and responsive service. Southwest Heritage Bank is a subsidiary of Bancorp 34, Inc. (OTC: BCTF). Member FDIC. Learn more at swhbank.com.

data.title: MMA.INC Provides NYSE American Listing Update
data.description:
New York, NY, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mixed Martial Arts Group Limited (NYSE American: MMA), doing business as MMA.INC, today advised that on November 25, 2026 it received a letter from NYSE Regulation notifying the Company that it is below compliance with the continued listing standard in Section 1003(a)(i) of the NYSE American Company Guide, which requires stockholders’ equity of US$2.0 million or more where a company has reported losses in two of its three most recent fiscal years. The notification relates to the stockholders’ equity position reported in the Company’s audited financial statements as at June 30, 2026. Release of this information is required by Sections 402(g) and 1009(j) of the Company Guide.

The Company is now subject to the procedures and requirements of Section 1009 of the Company Guide. The Company intends to submit a plan to NYSE American by December 25, 2026, setting out the actions it has taken or will take to regain compliance with the continued listing standards by May 25, 2028. If NYSE American accepts the plan, the Company will be subject to periodic review, including quarterly monitoring for compliance with the plan. If the plan is not accepted, or if the Company is not in compliance by May 25, 2028 or does not make progress consistent with the plan, NYSE American may initiate delisting proceedings.

Following the June 30, 2026 financial year end, the Company completed a US$4 million ordinary share equity capital raising at US$1.00 per share in August 2026. As announced on September 29, 2026, completed cost reduction actions increased the Company’s estimated total annualized cash operating cost reductions to over US$2.51 million, including over US$800,000 of additional annualized reductions implemented between July 1 and September 28, 2026.

The Company’s ordinary shares continue to trade on NYSE American. The notification has no effect on the Company’s business or operations, or on its reporting obligations under U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission rules.

For more information, visit www.mma.inc

Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as added by the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including statements regarding the Company’s intention to submit a compliance plan and its initiatives to strengthen its balance sheet. There can be no assurance that any plan submitted will be accepted, or that the Company will regain compliance within the plan period or at all. Actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties, including the Company’s ability to implement its compliance initiatives, continued operating losses and funding requirements, and the risk that estimated annualized cost reductions are not sustained or are offset by other expenditures. Additional risks are described under “Risk Factors” in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026. Forward-looking statements speak as of the date of this release, and the Company undertakes no obligation to update them except as required by applicable law.
